newsitem.title: UK: Gold trapped in sideways trade, platinum off highs.
newsitem.headline: Gold trapped in sideways trade, platinum off highs.

text.p: Gold, suffering in an unfavourable economic environment fort it, was trapped in a narrow range on Tuesday, running into selling pressure each time it surfaced above $342.00 a ounce.
Platinum shaved earlier gains after holding firm above $380.00 an ounce throughout the session amid concerns over delayed Russian supplies which led to a tight forward market.
Bullion fixed lower at $341.60 an ounce from $342.00 and by 1500 GMT was bid at $341.50 from a session high of $342.70. In New York Comex futures, the June contract lost $1.2 to $343.70.
Spot platinum was quoted $2.30 off its intraday high at $379.00. Palladium also trimmed gains to stand at $155.50.

"With platinum and palladium it can just be one non-delivery that does this," said one London dealer. "While non-deliveries are taking place the market is going to be tight and well-bid, but the minute they are not then it won't be," he added.
Analysts saw scope for a rally in platinum to $385.00 while the mystery surrounding Russian exports plagued the market.
Prices were lifted last week by rumours that Moscow might have delayed the delivery of a gold swap for PGM collateralised against a Swiss bank loan. The swap has not been confirmed.
Markets are also unnerved by disruptions caused by delays in Russian exports to Japan, the world's biggest PGM importer.
Platinum prices were still in a backwardation with swap rates at minus four percent, and lease rates around 9-9.5.
"The market is very speculative. We are advising customers to leave it alone," said one Swiss trader.
Gold encountered strong overhead resistance and dealers said failure to regain the $345.00 resistance could force it down to last week's lows of $337.50 and to test support at $336.15.
One dealer noted producer selling at $343.00. He expected that producers were likely to hedge more and further out.

"Each time it gets up there ($343) it gets stopped. It looks like the market is going to go and test lower levels. If it doesn't hold above $336 then I think we'll see it down to $300," said the dealer.
Technical analyst Karen Jones of Credit Suisse First Boston said if gold could maintain a foothold over $345.00 it would "at least suggest that it will hold sideways rather than go down."
Fears of interest hikes in the United States and rising stock prices are keeping hot money away from the gold market.
Silver was at $4.76/$4.78 an ounce. Failure to hold above the $4.60 area would signal a sell off to $4.33, Jones said.
